from solution import float_sort


def test_issue_example_given():
    """Example: float_sort sorts by float element to [('item3','24.5'),('item2','15.10'),('item1','12.20')]."""
    result = float_sort([('item1', '12.20'), ('item2', '15.10'), ('item3', '24.5')])
    # 24.5 > 15.10 > 12.20 so descending order is item3, item2, item1
    assert result == [('item3', '24.5'), ('item2', '15.10'), ('item1', '12.20')]


def test_issue_descending_by_float_value():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element in descending numeric order."""
    result = float_sort([('a', '1.00'), ('b', '3.50'), ('c', '2.25')])
    # 3.50 > 2.25 > 1.00 so order is b, c, a
    assert result == [('b', '3.50'), ('c', '2.25'), ('a', '1.00')]


def test_issue_numeric_not_string_order():
    """Sort by float element so '24.5' outranks '9.99' numerically."""
    result = float_sort([('item1', '9.99'), ('item2', '24.5'), ('item3', '12.20')])
    # 24.5 > 12.20 > 9.99 numerically, while string order would put '9.99' first
    assert result == [('item2', '24.5'), ('item3', '12.20'), ('item1', '9.99')]


def test_issue_empty_input():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element handles empty input."""
    result = float_sort([])
    # 0 items sorted is 0 items
    assert result == []


def test_issue_single_item():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element leaves one item unchanged."""
    result = float_sort([('only', '5.50')])
    # single value 5.50 needs no reordering
    assert result == [('only', '5.50')]


def test_issue_already_descending():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element keeps descending input as-is."""
    result = float_sort([('x', '30.00'), ('y', '20.00'), ('z', '10.00')])
    # 30.00 > 20.00 > 10.00 so order x, y, z is unchanged
    assert result == [('x', '30.00'), ('y', '20.00'), ('z', '10.00')]


def test_issue_ascending_input_reversed():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element reverses ascending input."""
    result = float_sort([('a', '1.10'), ('b', '2.20'), ('c', '3.30')])
    # 3.30 > 2.20 > 1.10 so order becomes c, b, a
    assert result == [('c', '3.30'), ('b', '2.20'), ('a', '1.10')]


def test_issue_negative_and_positive():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element orders negatives below positives."""
    result = float_sort([('a', '-2.5'), ('b', '3.0'), ('c', '-10.0')])
    # 3.0 > -2.5 > -10.0 so order is b, a, c
    assert result == [('b', '3.0'), ('a', '-2.5'), ('c', '-10.0')]


def test_issue_duplicate_prices_kept():
    """Sort a tuple by its float element keeps every item when prices tie."""
    result = float_sort([('a', '15.10'), ('b', '15.10'), ('c', '12.20')])
    # 15.10 == 15.10 > 12.20 so prices descending are 15.10, 15.10, 12.20
    assert [p for _, p in result] == ['15.10', '15.10', '12.20']


def test_contract_returns_list():
    """Example shows float_sort result equals a list."""
    result = float_sort([('item1', '12.20'), ('item2', '15.10')])
    # 15.10 > 12.20 checked elsewhere; here only the list type is checked
    assert isinstance(result, list)
